caption: Each candidate sentence is scored as its acoustic likelihood times its language-model prior; the largest product, W1 at 2.0 × 10⁻⁵, is chosen. Compare W2 and W3: W2 has the better acoustics (0.01 against 0.008) but the weaker prior (0.0005 against 0.002), so W3 wins that pair.

spec.title: Bayes rule on three candidates
spec.aria: One frame sequence X is scored against three candidate sentences, each score being acoustic likelihood times language-model prior: W1 gives 0.02 × 0.001 = 2.0 × 10⁻⁵, W2 gives 0.01 × 0.0005 = 5.0 × 10⁻⁶, W3 gives 0.008 × 0.002 = 1.6 × 10⁻⁵, and the largest product makes W1 the recognised sentence.
